title: BTS Pulls a Bathroom Prank to Hype Their New Song!
summary: Have you ever seen a boy band in a bathroom? BTS just made that happen—on purpose! The seven superstars put a hilarious ad in real newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle and New York Post. The headline screams: "BTS Seen in Bathroom Amid Mysterious Late-Night Gathering." The photo shows all seven members—RM, Jung Kook, V, Jimin, Suga, Jin, and j-hope—standing at urinals with their backs to us. It looks like they're taking a group bathroom break! But it's all a clever trick. The ad is really for their new single, "NORMAL," which drops on Friday, July 17, first on Spotify. The song is about the space between being in the spotlight and having quiet, normal moments. It mixes calm singing and rapping with a beat that hits hard, plus some trippy guitar sounds. The ad copy even jokes that a spokesperson "declined to comment" on the mysterious photo. Talk about commitment to a bit! BTS is also about to play huge shows in France and then headline the first-ever FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show with Justin Bieber, Madonna, and Shakira. Their last single, "SWIM," swam all the way to No. 1. Now they're proving that even bathroom breaks can be world-class promotion.
why_it_matters: This shows that even top celebrities use funny pranks to get people talking, and creativity can grab everyone's attention, just like when you make a silly video for a school project.

keywords.explanation: Urinals are special wall-mounted toilets for boys and men to pee into while standing up.
Trippy means something that sounds or looks strange and dreamlike, like a weird guitar effect.
A spokesperson is a person whose job is to speak to the public for a company or group.
Halftime is the short break in the middle of a sports game, often with a show.
Promotion means actions to make more people know about and buy a product or song.
A bit is a short comedy act or joke that performers commit to.

background_read: BTS is a hugely famous K-pop boy band from South Korea with millions of fans worldwide, often called ARMY.
The FIFA World Cup Final is the biggest soccer match on Earth, and for the first time it will feature a halftime show with music stars.
K-pop groups like BTS are known for creative, funny ads and surprises to get people excited about new music before it releases.
Article_Structure: WHO: The seven members of BTS (RM, Jung Kook, V, Jimin, Suga, Jin, and j-hope)
WHAT: They placed a humorous newspaper ad showing them in a bathroom to promote their new single
WHERE: In major real newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle and New York Post
WHY: To build excitement for their song 'NORMAL' and highlight their upcoming performances, including the FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show

perspectives.description: Fans find the prank hilarious and original, making them even more excited to hear 'NORMAL' and see BTS perform soon.
Some people might think bathroom humor is childish or that the ad is just a distraction and doesn't say much about the actual music.
It's a clever way to stand out in a busy news world where artists need unique stunts to make headlines and spark conversations.
